elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 as rendered still binds Customer: "neither Ono or its Affiliates ... shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory: (i) a product that includes ... an agent that is a [ * ] (other than Binimetinib), or (ii) ... (other than Encorafenib)". The redline narrows but does not delete the covenant on Customer, so the preferred no-restriction outcome is not achieved.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: "Competing Product" is defined by compound class, not by a named product: "a product that includes, as an active pharmaceutical ingredient, an agent that is a [ * ] (other than Binimetinib)" and the definitional tail "'[ * ]' means a compound that [ * ]". The covenant therefore reaches every product in an entire (and, on the face of the operative text, redacted/undetermined) mechanism class, not a single named competing product. Naming Binimetinib/Encorafenib only as exclusions does not name the restricted product.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Ono's and its Affiliates' obligations under this Section 8.2 shall apply only during the term of this Agreement", and the prior post-termination extension ("prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect") has been struck.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "shall in no event extend beyond the twelve (12) month anniversary of the Effective Date" — an express outer cap of twelve months.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Inserted carve-out: "shall not restrict (i) Ono's or its Affiliates' internal research or Development activities".
Inserted carve-out: "(ii) any product or program acquired by Ono or its Affiliates through any acquisition of or merger with a Third Party".

reasons: Preferred level not reached and not attempted: an operative non-compete on Customer survives in Section 8.2.

Fallback level is incomplete on one element. The scope prong is class-based, not product-named: the covenant catches any product whose API is an agent within the redacted "[ * ]" class, with only Binimetinib and Encorafenib carved out. To repair, amend the chapeau/definition so Ono's obligation is limited to an expressly named competing product (or an expressly named single compound), e.g. "Ono's obligation under this Section 8.2 shall apply only to [named product]", rather than to an entire compound class whose definition is not ascertainable from the operative text.

Duration, term-limitation and both carve-outs are properly rendered in operative language (not merely promised in the comment): term-only limitation, a twelve-month outer cap, internal research/Development carve-out, and an acquisition/merger carve-out.

Minimality holds: the only deletion is the post-termination extension sentence, which is necessary to reach "during the term only"; Array's reciprocal restriction, the royalty-termination consequence sentence and Array's immediate termination right are all retained; no survival tails, expense language or unrelated procedure was added.

Intent preserved: the retained chapeau "Prior to the [ * ]" continues to bind Array, the inserted sentence narrows only Ono's side without contradicting it, and no cross-reference (including Article XIV's reference to Section 8.2) is left dangling. Note the twelve-month cap is anchored to the Effective Date rather than to the start of the restricted period; if the Effective Date has already passed at signing this reduces the restriction to near zero, which Vendor may resist — anchoring to the Effective Date is acceptable under the checklist but expect pushback.
